samples.summary: `--round N` bypasses the enforced self-review bound entirely and silently overwrites an existing round's verdicts
samples.evidence: Line 979: `const round = args.round === undefined ? nextRound(onDisk) : Number(args.round);` and line 987: `const spentRound = args.fresh ? Math.max(round, nextRound(onDiskBefore)) : round;`. When `--round` is supplied explicitly and `--fresh` is not, `spentRound` is simply the *requested* number, never the number of rounds actually spent. So on a branch with three real rounds on disk, `node spec-to-pr.mjs review --round 1` gives `roundBoundNotice(1) === ""`, the refusal at line 989 never fires, and a fourth round runs — with no `--force`, no warning, and no carry-forward (line 1055: `const prior = round > 1 ? priorFindingsFor(base, round) : []` yields `[]`). This is precisely the failure the `--fresh` guard was just written to close (lines 980-986: "a fourth round presents itself as a clean first one… `--force` stays the only door through"), reached through a second, undefended door. It is also destructive: `mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true })` at line 1041 reuses the existing `round-1` directory and `review-panel.mjs` rewrites each lens's `verdict.json` in place, destroying the round-1 verdicts that later rounds' `pickLatestVerdicts` reaches back for when a lens crashes. `roundBoundNotice`'s own docblock (lines 224-226) asserts `--fresh` is not that door while saying nothing about `--round`, so the invariant the module claims to enforce does not hold.

samples.summary: `--fresh` deletes every round directory before the `--rebuttals` file is validated, so a typo'd path destroys the verdicts and then aborts
samples.evidence: The delete loop runs at lines 1009-1013, but `prepareRoundInputs` / `readRebuttalRecords` — which `throw` on a missing, unparseable or empty `--rebuttals` file and lead to `fail(e.message)` — is not reached until line 1058. So `review --fresh --rebuttals typo.json` removes every `round-N` directory and *then* exits 1 without running a review, leaving the branch with no rounds and no replacement. This is the same ordering defect the comment at lines 1003-1008 says was just fixed for the bound refusal ("the refusal was destructive"), and the comment at lines 1049-1054 explicitly states the intent that argument errors be reported before anything expensive or irreversible happens. The rebuttals validation (and `reviewArgsError`'s other checks) should precede the destructive `rmSync` loop.

samples.summary: The "re-run for round N+1" instruction is wrong for exactly the round the round-counting rule exists to handle
samples.evidence: Line 1115 prints `re-run for round ${round + 1}` unconditionally on a blocking round. But `nextRound` (lines 180-186) deliberately does NOT advance past a round in which no lens produced a usable verdict — the documented HTTP 429 / quota-outage case, where every lens writes `{ valid: false }` (review-panel.mjs:2840) and `verdictProduced` returns false. Such a round *is* blocking (every lens concludes `failure`), so this message fires, tells the developer the next run will be round N+1, and the next invocation in fact reuses round N and overwrites the directory. The one case the counter was specially built for is the one the printed guidance describes incorrectly.

samples.summary: `carryForwardFindings` spreads `mergedFrom` through raw, diverging from the cloud projection it claims to mirror
samples.evidence: Line 174: `mergedFrom: Array.isArray(f.mergedFrom) ? f.mergedFrom : undefined`. The docblock two lines above states "PROJECT, never spread… a spread carries every key a lens chose to write", yet each `mergedFrom` entry is carried verbatim. The cloud copy this function exists to mirror rebuilds every entry from an explicit field list (.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:1028: `m.mergedFrom.slice(0, 5).map((m) => ({ severity: norm(m.severity), summary: trim(m.summary, 500), adjudication: … }))`). Consequence: arbitrary model-written keys inside `mergedFrom` (including a nested `infra: true`, which `isInfraRecord` only inspects at the top level) reach the next round's verifier input locally but not in the cloud, and `upheldCount` (rebuttal.mjs:424) reads `mergedFrom[].adjudication` from an unbounded, unnormalised list. The new drift-guard test (prior-findings.test.mjs) only asserts the two *selection* filters, so this projection divergence is uncovered.

samples.summary: Round directory names are parsed to a number and then re-synthesised, so a zero-padded name is counted but never resolvable
samples.evidence: `roundsIn` (line 157) extracts `Number(m[1])` from a name matched by `/^round-(\d+)$/`, and every consumer then rebuilds the path as `round-${round}`: `roundsOnDisk` line 834, `priorFindingsFor` line 865, `roundDirsToClear` line 733. A directory named `round-01` therefore reports as round 1, but `path.join(base, "round-1")` does not exist — `roundsOnDisk` swallows the `ENOENT` and reports zero lenses, `priorFindingsFor` carries nothing from it, and `--fresh` issues `rmSync(base + "/round-1", { force: true })`, a no-op that leaves the directory behind forever. Carrying the matched entry name alongside the number would remove the round-trip.

samples.summary: `priorFindingsFor`'s documented "never throws" contract is broken by the unguarded `readdirSync(base)` inside `roundsOnDisk`
samples.evidence: The docblock at lines 855-858 says "Never throws", but `roundsOnDisk` (line 833) calls `readdirSync(base)` outside any `try`. If `base` has been removed or replaced by a file between the guard at line 925-966 and this read (or by any other caller of the exported helper — it is exported and unit-tested independently), the call throws `ENOENT`/`ENOTDIR` and propagates out of `priorFindingsFor` as an uncaught stack rather than the empty carry-forward every other failure direction on this path degrades to. `roundsOnDisk`'s own docblock (lines 825-830) justifies guarding the per-round `readdirSync` for exactly this reason but leaves the outer one bare.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo. At spec-to-pr.mjs:979 an explicit --round is taken verbatim, and at :987 spentRound is only raised to nextRound(onDiskBefore) when args.fresh is set; without --fresh spentRound is the requested number, so roundBoundNotice (:228-229 returns "" for round <= MAX_SELF_REVIEW_ROUNDS=3) produces no notice and the refusal at :989 never fires. reviewArgsError (:605-615) validates --round only as a positive integer and never compares it to roundsOnDisk, so `review --round 1` on a branch with three spent rounds runs an unbounded fourth round. It is also destructive: :1041 mkdirSync(dir,{recursive:true}) reuses the existing round-1 directory and review-panel.mjs:3433-3445 rewrites each lens's verdict.json in place, destroying the verdicts priorFindingsFor/pickLatestVerdicts (:860-869, :200-214) reach back for when a lens crashed in a later round; and :1055 yields an empty carry-forward for round 1. This contradicts the module's own stated invariant at :224-226 and :985-986 that --force is the only door past the bound. No guard elsewhere closes it, and existing tests (spec-to-pr.test.mjs:703-746, :330-342) cover only the --fresh door and --round parsing.
